I added Student and Partner, and each customer's discount now comes with its receipt line. All 11 tests pass: the 2 existing ones and 9 new ones.

**What changed** (in `Shop/Pricing.cs`)
- **Student:** 10% off, never more than 30 per order. Receipt: `Student: 10% off, max 30`.
- **Partner:** 10% off up to 1,000, and 15% off the whole order above 1,000. Exactly 1,000 gets 10%. Receipt: `Partner: 10% off, 15% off above 1,000`.
- **Receipt line:** `PriceCalculator.DiscountReceiptLine(order)` returns one line per customer type. `Loyal: 5% off` matches your example.

**Choices you may want to change**
- Your examples didn't cover Regular customers, so I gave them `Regular: no discount`. If they shouldn't get a line at all, that's a one-word change.
- I wrote the Partner wording myself, since you didn't give one.

**Design**
Each customer type now has one small rule that holds both its discount and its receipt text, so the two can't get out of step. Since a new customer type is coming every month, adding one is two edits next to each other: a new value in `CustomerType` and one new line in `PriceCalculator.RuleFor`. Each rule can also be tested on its own.

I added one new type, `DiscountRule`, rather than a separate class per customer type. Each rule is a line or two of logic, so a class per customer would add more code than it holds. If a future rule needs more data, such as a minimum basket or a promo code, that's the point to switch to a class per type.

**Tests added**
- Student, under the cap and at the cap (1,000 → pays 970).
- Partner, at exactly 1,000 (10%) and at 1,200 (15% of the whole order → pays 1,020).
- The receipt line for all four customer types.
- A check that every customer type has a rule. The code compiles even if a new type has no rule and would only fail when that customer orders, so this test catches it first.
